passages: Meta has officially launched a new pair of camera-free smart glasses at Meta Connect.
Dubbed “Ray-Ban Meta Audio,” these glasses ditch the privacy nightmare of cameras on your temples and offer an audio-only experience.
The company has also launched new camera-equipped models and a “Muse Charm” accessory.

Meta ( META ) launched three new pairs of smart glasses during the company's Meta Connect conference on Wednesday. CEO Mark Zuckerberg took the stage to show off the trio of devices, which includes the company's first Meta VR Glasses, the camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses, and the third generation of its Ray-Ban Meta glasses. The $1,299 Meta VR Glasses are the standout of the trio, offering virtual reality capabilities in a glasses-style design, which makes other VR headsets look ancient by comparison. On sale in spring 2027, the company says the high-tech eyewear is five times lighter than its Meta Quest 3 headset, and features a 5K display for watching shows and 3D movies, playing games, and working. Because you're looking at two screens, there are external cameras so that you can see the world around you while wearing them. The glass's computing components, battery, and storage are housed in a separate dedicated puck that tethers to the spectacles, helping to ensure they're light enough to wear for long periods. To navigate, you use hand gestures or can speak to the on-board Muse AI agent. And unlike in the Muse app, you'll see a fully rendered version of your custom Muse avatar. For film buffs, Meta says the VR Glasses are the first-ever IMAX Enhanced-certified VR device, allowing customers to watch IMAX movies at home. The company is also partnering with Disney+ ( DIS ) to give users access to movies like "The Avengers" and "Black Panther." Meta says it's working to bring Amazon's ( AMZN ) Prime Video, Google's ( GOOG , GOOGL ) YouTube, and other streamers to the platform, as well. In the office, the Meta VR Glasses can display a single large virtual display or several smaller ones, allowing you to switch between apps throughout the day. Flat surfaces turn into virtual keyboards and mice, letting you navigate and type documents without the need for secondary accessories. For gamers, Microsoft ( MSFT ) is bringing its Xbox Cloud Gaming service to the glasses, so users can play on the go. Meta is also introducing what it calls its hologram calling technology. Users take a picture of themselves in the Meta AI app, which then creates a full-body digital version of them that they can use to make video calls with friends and family while wearing the glasses. Apple has a similar feature for its Vision Pro headset. In addition to the Meta VR Glasses, Meta also unveiled the company's $349 Ray-Ban Meta Audio smart glasses. Unlike the standard Ray-Ban Meta glasses, the Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses come sans cameras, making them look far more like a standard pair of Ray-Bans. The lack of cameras also means the Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses are lighter and can offer up to 12 hours of battery life. As with the original Ray-Ban Meta glasses, the audio-only versions allow you to listen to music without headphones and chat with Meta's AI. This time, however, that comes in the form of the Muse AI agent . Removing the cameras from the glasses also eliminates one of the main criticisms of Meta's smart glasses — that users can record people without their knowledge. While Meta has outfitted its Ray-Ban Meta glasses with an LED light that lets people know when the glasses are recording or taking a picture, there have been instances of owners tampering with the indicator. The backlash has prompted cities , states, and businesses worldwide to restrict the use of camera-equipped smart glasses in certain situations. Meta isn't doing away with camera-based glasses, though. The company also debuted its $449 third-generation Ray-Ban Meta glasses, which sport a longer battery life and improved microphones. The company has also updated its own line of its Meta Glasses, which are separate from the Ray-Ban Meta glasses, starting at $249. Zuckerberg's Meta is the global smart glasses leader, accounting for 68.7% of global shipments in Q2 2026, according to the International Data Corporation (IDC) . But Meta is about to get some fellow deep-pocketed rivals with Samsung and Google preparing to launch their own glasses later this fall . The smart glasses, with designs from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, will run on Google's Android XR, which it developed with Samsung and Qualcomm. Snap ( SNAP ) is also rolling out its Specs AR glasses, though they'll cost a $2,195 . Apple is also rumored to be working on its own smart glasses, with Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reporting that the company will debut the product in late 2027. sources.title: Meta Announces Ray-Ban Meta Audio, Its First Smart Glasses Without A Camera - Engadget
passages: Invasive use of Meta's camera-enabled smart glasses has earned them the moniker "pervert glasses," and the company has prepped a solution for Meta Connect 2026: Ray-Ban Meta Audio, smart glasses that ditch cameras entirely to focus on audio features and AI.

Naturally, Meta doesn't characterize the new glasses as a response to public backlash — though they are making it harder to use the camera-equipped kind for surreptitious filming — but rather as an acknowledgement that audio has always been its smart glasses' most popular feature.

extraction.body: Invasive use of Meta's camera-enabled smart glasses has earned them the moniker "pervert glasses," and the company has prepped a solution for Meta Connect 2026: Ray-Ban Meta Audio, smart glasses that ditch cameras entirely to focus on audio features and AI. Naturally, Meta doesn't characterize the new glasses as a response to public backlash — though they are making it harder to use the camera-equipped kind for surreptitious filming — but rather as an acknowledgement that audio has always been its smart glasses' most popular feature. The new frames are capable of taking calls, letting you respond to messages with your voice and playing back podcasts and music without cutting you off from the rest of the world. They're also a way to access Meta AI for things like live translation and real-time answers to questions. Another way of looking at the Ray-Ban Meta Audio is as a way to get many of the hardware improvements of the company's latest models, without the extra baggage. Meta says they'll last up to 12 hours on a single charge, with an additional 48 hours available if you use their charging case. They also include the same fit adjustments as the company's previous frames, with the option for adjustable temple tips, customizable nose pads and overextension hinges (hinges with springs that can accommodate a wider selection of head shapes and widths) for improved comfort. Ditching the cameras also means the glasses are lighter at 43 grams; Meta's other models weigh anywhere from 49.2 grams (the recent Optics glasses ) to 69 grams (the largest size of Meta Ray-Ban Display ). The real win for Meta and anyone potentially curious about the company's smart glasses is that removing the camera and recording light makes these new frames look even more normal than before. Unless you clocked the slightly larger temples and cut-outs for speakers, you might not know the Ray-Ban Meta Audio are anything other than Ray-Bans. The company is selling the new glasses in two new styles, a rectangular option called Burbank and a retro-inspired style called Clubmaster, both in 23 colors and lens combinations. They also support a range of optical prescriptions, according to the company. At this moment in Meta's public perception , releasing the Ray-Ban Meta Audio isn't likely to convert critics, but they could convince someone uncomfortable with the optics of smart glasses in general. Unless of course Meta does something to make people even more mad, like actually releasing the facial recognition feature it was previously testing . The Ray-Ban Meta Audio ship October 13 and are available to pre-order today starting at $349.

extraction.body: Walking around Meta Connect 2026, everyone’s sporting smart glasses in all sorts of shapes, colors, and sizes. It’s a marked difference here, a tech bubble where “pervert glasses” are not a concern. Outside Connect, the public backlash against wearable surveillance tech — a catchall term that encompasses not just smart glasses, but also smartwatches and AI pendants — is gaining steam. So it’s incredibly curious timing that this year, the company is launching Ray-Ban Meta Audio Glasses: smart glasses infused with Meta AI, but with no camera for recording others. Audio-only glasses have been years in the making. “Three years ago, it wasn’t clear if AI glasses were going to be a thing. Back then, every other company was backing out of the space,” says Alex Himel, Meta’s vice president of wearables. “Then two years ago, we saw that audio was the top use case, the biggest potential for AI, and that it should work well in a pair of audio glasses.” [Image: There are multiple combinations of colors and lenses across two styles for the audio-only glasses. Open-ear audio is the least controversial part of the Ray-Bans — and the thing everyone can agree is convenient. Himel says that by removing the cameras, Meta could “rearchitect” the glasses. “That allowed us to take a lot of electronics out of the front frame and have a lot more design flexibility.” The audio-only models start at 43 grams — heavier than normal wire-frame glasses, but noticeably lighter than the roughly 50g Ray-Ban Meta Gen 2 and the 69g Meta Ray-Ban Display. There are 23 color and lens combinations, and they can support the same wider prescription range as the Ray-Ban Meta Optics lineup. Even more so than the standard Meta Ray-Bans, these look and wear like normal glasses. And with a $349 starting price, they’re cheaper too. Free of a power-hungry camera, the battery lasts an estimated 12 hours on a single charge. The most technical things you can do with them are interact with Meta AI, take phone calls, and listen to podcasts or music. Regardless of how one might feel about Meta, it’s fair to guess most people would feel less like a creeper wearing these. Meta Glasses and Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 I feel differently slipping on the new Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3. Partly because the camera is back in play, partly because the pair Meta gives me is the new aviator style with transition lenses. The third-generation glasses feature fairly minor refinements. The temple arms, like the audio-only glasses, are adjustable for a better fit. All sound will now be captured in Dolby Atmos for spatial audio. That’s neat if I’m in my quiet hotel room, but it’s harder to appreciate when reviewing footage amid the hustle and bustle of Meta Connect. Meta ( META ) launched three new pairs of smart glasses during the company's Meta Connect conference on Wednesday. CEO Mark Zuckerberg took the stage to show off the trio of devices, which includes the company's first Meta VR Glasses, the camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses, and the third generation of its Ray-Ban Meta glasses. On sale in spring 2027, the company says the high-tech eyewear is five times lighter than its Meta Quest 3 headset, and features a 5K display for watching shows and 3D movies, playing games, and working. Because you're looking at two screens, there are external cameras so that you can see the world around you while wearing them. The glass's computing components, battery, and storage are housed in a separate dedicated puck that tethers to the spectacles, helping to ensure they're light enough to wear for long periods. To navigate, you use hand gestures or can speak to the on-board Muse AI agent. And unlike in the Muse app, you'll see a fully rendered version of your custom Muse avatar. For film buffs, Meta says the VR Glasses are the first-ever IMAX Enhanced-certified VR device, allowing customers to watch IMAX movies at home. The company is also partnering with Disney+ ( DIS ) to give users access to movies like "The Avengers" and "Black Panther." Meta says it's working to bring Amazon's ( AMZN ) Prime Video, Google's ( GOOG , GOOGL ) YouTube, and other streamers to the platform, as well. In the office, the Meta VR Glasses can display a single large virtual display or several smaller ones, allowing you to switch between apps throughout the day. Flat surfaces turn into virtual keyboards and mice, letting you navigate and type documents without the need for secondary accessories. For gamers, Microsoft ( MSFT ) is bringing its Xbox Cloud Gaming service to the glasses, so users can play on the go. Meta is also introducing what it calls its hologram calling technology. Users take a picture of themselves in the Meta AI app, which then creates a full-body digital version of them that they can use to make video calls with friends and family while wearing the glasses. Apple has a similar feature for its Vision Pro headset. In addition to the Meta VR Glasses, Meta also unveiled the company's $349 Ray-Ban Meta Audio smart glasses. Unlike the standard Ray-Ban Meta glasses, the Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses come sans cameras, making them look far more like a standard pair of Ray-Bans. The lack of cameras also means the Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses are lighter and can offer up to 12 hours of battery life. As with the original Ray-Ban Meta glasses, the audio-only versions allow you to listen to music without headphones and chat with Meta's AI. This time, however, that comes in the form of the Muse AI agent . Removing the cameras from the glasses also eliminates one of the main criticisms of Meta's smart glasses — that users can record people without their knowledge. While Meta has outfitted its Ray-Ban Meta glasses with an LED light that lets people know when the glasses are recording or taking a picture, there have been instances of owners tampering with the indicator. The backlash has prompted cities , states, and businesses worldwide to restrict the use of camera-equipped smart glasses in certain situations. Meta isn't doing away with camera-based glasses, though. The company also debuted its $449 third-generation Ray-Ban Meta glasses, which sport a longer battery life and improved microphones. The company has also updated its own line of its Meta Glasses, which are separate from the Ray-Ban Meta glasses, starting at $249. Zuckerberg's Meta is the global smart glasses leader, accounting for 68.7% of global shipments in Q2 2026, according to the International Data Corporation (IDC) . But Meta is about to get some fellow deep-pocketed rivals with Samsung and Google preparing to launch their own glasses later this fall . The smart glasses, with designs from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, will run on Google's Android XR, which it developed with Samsung and Qualcomm. Snap ( SNAP ) is also rolling out its Specs AR glasses, though they'll cost a $2,195 . Apple is also rumored to be working on its own smart glasses, with Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reporting that the company will debut the product in late 2027. passages: Invasive use of Meta's camera-enabled smart glasses has earned them the moniker "pervert glasses," and the company has prepped a solution for Meta Connect 2026: Ray-Ban Meta Audio, smart glasses that ditch cameras entirely to focus on audio features and AI.

Naturally, Meta doesn't characterize the new glasses as a response to public backlash — though they are making it harder to use the camera-equipped kind for surreptitious filming — but rather as an acknowledgement that audio has always been its smart glasses' most popular feature.

extraction.body: Invasive use of Meta's camera-enabled smart glasses has earned them the moniker "pervert glasses," and the company has prepped a solution for Meta Connect 2026: Ray-Ban Meta Audio, smart glasses that ditch cameras entirely to focus on audio features and AI. Naturally, Meta doesn't characterize the new glasses as a response to public backlash — though they are making it harder to use the camera-equipped kind for surreptitious filming — but rather as an acknowledgement that audio has always been its smart glasses' most popular feature. The new frames are capable of taking calls, letting you respond to messages with your voice and playing back podcasts and music without cutting you off from the rest of the world. They're also a way to access Meta AI for things like live translation and real-time answers to questions. Another way of looking at the Ray-Ban Meta Audio is as a way to get many of the hardware improvements of the company's latest models, without the extra baggage. Meta says they'll last up to 12 hours on a single charge, with an additional 48 hours available if you use their charging case. They also include the same fit adjustments as the company's previous frames, with the option for adjustable temple tips, customizable nose pads and overextension hinges (hinges with springs that can accommodate a wider selection of head shapes and widths) for improved comfort. Ditching the cameras also means the glasses are lighter at 43 grams; Meta's other models weigh anywhere from 49.2 grams (the recent Optics glasses ) to 69 grams (the largest size of Meta Ray-Ban Display ). The real win for Meta and anyone potentially curious about the company's smart glasses is that removing the camera and recording light makes these new frames look even more normal than before. Unless you clocked the slightly larger temples and cut-outs for speakers, you might not know the Ray-Ban Meta Audio are anything other than Ray-Bans. The company is selling the new glasses in two new styles, a rectangular option called Burbank and a retro-inspired style called Clubmaster, both in 23 colors and lens combinations. They also support a range of optical prescriptions, according to the company. At this moment in Meta's public perception , releasing the Ray-Ban Meta Audio isn't likely to convert critics, but they could convince someone uncomfortable with the optics of smart glasses in general. Unless of course Meta does something to make people even more mad, like actually releasing the facial recognition feature it was previously testing . The Ray-Ban Meta Audio ship October 13 and are available to pre-order today starting at $349.

extraction.body: Meta announced today a series of AI-powered devices, including the Muse Charm, a palm-sized gadget designed specifically for its new Muse AI assistant. Here are the details. Meta kicked off its Meta Connect 2026 event today, its yearly showcase for new AI technologies, wearables, and VR products. Last year, the biggest announcement was the Meta Ray-Ban Display , the company’s first smart glasses with a built-in display that can show messages, navigation, Meta AI responses, and more. At the time, Meta’s AI-powered glasses lineup was already gaining significant traction, with Meta and EssilorLuxottica going on to sell more than 7 million units for the year. Since then, Meta’s camera-equipped glasses have faced growing scrutiny over privacy and ethics, as there has been no shortage of discussions involving privacy, ethics, and the general pushback on AI. Today, Meta announced the Ray-Ban Meta Audio , its first pair of camera-free smart glasses, which starts at $349 and will be available beginning October 13. The Ray-Ban Meta Audio retains features such as music and podcast playback, calls, and live translation, offering many of the same audio features as Meta’s camera-equipped glasses. They also support Muse , Meta’s recently launched personal AI agent. That said, Meta also announced the Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 3) tonight, featuring a slimmer design, up to nine hours of battery life, and a new action button, while retaining the 12MP camera and 3K video recording introduced with the previous generation. The new action button can be customized in the Meta AI app to provide one-touch access to Meta AI or other features, such as live translation. The Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 3) is available today, starting at $449. In tonight’s event, the company also announced the Meta VR Glasses , a roughly 100-gram VR headset designed to look and feel more like a pair of glasses. The device features what Meta calls a “5K Infinite Display built on micro-OLED panels,” built-in Meta AI, eye and hand tracking, and a separate pocketable puck that handles processing, battery, and storage. Meta is pitching the VR Glasses as a personal cinema, gaming device, and workspace. They are also the first IMAX Enhanced-certified VR device, with support for 3D movies and immersive live sports. Alongside the Meta VR Glasses, the company also introduced a new hologram feature that can create a photorealistic avatar that reflects a user’s real-time expressions and reactions during video calls. Meta says that a version of the feature is also coming to Meta Ray-Ban Display , where users can create a digital version of their face for hands-free video calls, beginning with WhatsApp. The Meta VR Glasses will go on sale in spring 2027 for $1,299.99. Rounding up tonight’s glassware news, Meta also expanded its own Meta Glasses lineup with two new styles, Capri and Nova, a new collection designed with LISA, and the $249 Meta Adventurer, its most affordable pair of smart glasses yet. The company also introduced a limited-edition Meta Fury model and a new Ivory colorway for its Kylie Jenner collaboration. At tonight’s event, Meta also announced the Muse Charm, a palm-sized device built specifically around its recently launched Muse personal AI agent. Meta launched Muse earlier this month, and the app has since risen to the No. 1 spot on both the U.S. App Store and Google Play. According to Bloomberg , the Muse Charm was developed by Meta’s new design lab, led by former Apple interface design chief Alan Dye, alongside the company’s Superintelligence AI group. The Muse Charm, which Meta refers to as a “holdable,” features a roughly 2-inch OLED touchscreen with a customizable Muse character at the center of the interface. Users can change its appearance, outfits, voice, and other attributes, and interact with Muse directly through the device. Zuck just revealed a Muse-powered tamagotchi 😳 Muse Charm. He says they will ship before the holidays. No one here expected this. pic.twitter.com/19leWPk77x The device also includes front- and rear-facing cameras, speakers, microphones, 5G connectivity, and a USB-C port. The cameras can capture photos and videos, but Bloomberg reports they are primarily intended to provide Muse with visual context for analysis and AI-assisted actions, rather than to serve as traditional cameras. Users set up and sync the Charm through the Muse app on iPhone or Android. Two Charm devices can also recognize and interact with each other when placed nearby. Meta plans to begin selling the Muse Charm in December. The company has not yet announced a price, but Bloomberg reports that it is expected to cost roughly as much as a smartwatch. extraction.body: Its popular Meta Ray-Ban glasses are now in their third generation, but two new models steal the show: a powerful, slimmed-down version of Meta's Quest headsets capable of virtual and augmented reality modes, and a camera-free pair of Ray-Ban–branded smart glasses, called Ray-Ban Meta Audio. Meta is also bringing its Muse AI agent to its smart glasses platform. Meta VR Glasses The next evolution of Meta’s Quest VR headset is something truly different. Instead of a heavy helmet-like headset, the new Meta VR Glasses look like big goggles. They’re five times lighter than the Meta Quest 3. They sit on the nose, right in front of your face like glasses, with no headstrap needed. They look and feel more like the virtual display glasses made by companies like Viture, and what Xreal’s Project Aura seems to be shaping up to be—lightweight mixed-reality lenses that let you access virtual spaces without the burden of a VR headset. There are no included controllers, though the device can connect to Meta’s previous Quest controllers or gamepads like an Xbox controller. Form a fist and flick your thumb up or down to scroll the screen. Small prescription lens inserts can be magnetically clipped inside the lenses. (Meta has not shared how much those will cost.) The software is the same that runs on Meta’s Quest VR devices, so movie and game titles in the Quest ecosystem will work on the VR Glasses. The VR Glasses can also display a virtual keyboard on a surface in front of you, then use the embedded cameras to track specific finger placements. The only immediate downside compared to other VR headsets—at least that I could tell from a brief demo at Meta Connect—is that the VR glasses don’t cover your entire field of vision, so it doesn’t feel as immersive as a traditional VR headset. Meta says the VR Glasses cost $1,300 and will ship in the spring of 2027. Ray-Ban Meta Audio Meta has spent the past few months being absolutely pummeled by controversy about the privacy issues inherent in its camera-enabled smart glasses. The Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses have all the audio capabilities of a standard pair of Meta’s smart glasses, minus image and video capture. At 43 grams, they’re also lighter than the others. They come in 23 different color and style options, including the retro Ray-Ban Clubmaster frame and a more rectangular Burbank. The Audio glasses cost $349 and are available for preorder now. Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 Meta's flagship line of smart glasses is getting a “Gen 3” upgrade. They have 12-MP cameras, like last year, plus 3K Dolby Atmos–enabled video capture. The glasses will get up to nine hours of battery life, two more than their predecessors. A new hearing aid feature called Hearing Enhancement uses the speakers in Meta's glasses to enhance speech and audio around the wearer, similar to the Nuance glasses from EssilorLuxottica. Earlier this summer, Meta debuted smart glasses under its own branding, which cost a little less but were functionally identical to the Ray-Ban models. Now, it is already following them up with Gen 3 versions. These Meta-branded glasses come in a cat-eye shape called Capri and a rounder lens called Nova. The Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 glasses start at $449. The Meta-branded Gen 3 glasses are also on sale now for $299. Muse Charm For folks who don't wear glasses, Meta has teased a new product altogether: the Muse Charm. Zuckerberg says it's the “fastest way to talk to your Muse,” referring to the company's AI agent, and show it the world around you. That likely means it has a camera on the back. Zuckerberg says Meta still needs to finalize the hardware, but plans to have it ready by the holiday season. Meta Ray-Ban Display Meta's Display glasses are also getting some updates. With the implementation of Meta AI, users can create photorealistic holograms of their faces, which can be helpful for video calls.

passages: Confirming earlier reports , Meta announced its first pair of camera-free AI glasses, the clunkily named Ray-Ban Meta Audio, at its Connect 2026 conference on Wednesday.

Designed to combat criticism around the more malicious use cases for AI glasses, which saw them nicknamed “pervert glasses” by some, the new devices will be audio-only, offering the ability to listen to music and podcasts, take calls, translate speech, and communicate with Meta’s AI assistant, Muse.
These will have a 12 MP camera that supports 3K Ultra HD video, a six-mic array, and up to nine hours of battery life.

While Meta today offers a range of AI glasses in a variety of styles, colors, and capabilities, the audio-only glasses could help the brand recover from some of the reputational damage after critics pointed out how people , often men , were using AI glasses to record videos without subjects’ consent.
Meta attempted to mitigate this issue with an update that would disable the camera if the LED light that indicated the glasses were recording was ever tampered with.

The glasses Meta launched with EssilorLuxottica will also see an expanded lineup of styles and colors as well as a new partnership with singer Lisa, which follows the company’s earlier brand partnership with Kylie Jenner.

The company also teased other coming updates, including support for Dolby Atmos Capture, a feature that picks the best photo from multiple frames, an option to choose landscape or portrait modes, hearing enhancements for those with hearing loss, more detailed responses, different audio modes, customizable controls, and something called “private processing” that Meta claims will prevent the company from seeing your data.

coreStoryFacts.text: Today, Meta announced the Ray-Ban Meta Audio , its first pair of camera-free smart glasses, which starts at $349 and will be available beginning October 13.
Meta announced today a series of AI-powered devices, including the Muse Charm, a palm-sized gadget designed specifically for its new Muse AI assistant.
They also support Muse , Meta’s recently launched personal AI agent.

The device features what Meta calls a “5K Infinite Display built on micro-OLED panels,” built-in Meta AI, eye and hand tracking, and a separate pocketable puck that handles processing, battery, and storage.
At the time, Meta’s AI-powered glasses lineup was already gaining significant traction, with Meta and EssilorLuxottica going on to sell more than 7 million units for the year.
Since then, Meta’s camera-equipped glasses have faced growing scrutiny over privacy and ethics, as there has been no shortage of discussions involving privacy, ethics, and the general pushback on AI.
Meta launched Muse earlier this month, and the app has since risen to the No.
Users can change its appearance, outfits, voice, and other attributes, and interact with Muse directly through the device.
The company has not yet announced a price, but Bloomberg reports that it is expected to cost roughly as much as a smartwatch.
Meta is pitching the VR Glasses as a personal cinema, gaming device, and workspace.
They are also the first IMAX Enhanced-certified VR device, with support for 3D movies and immersive live sports.
Meta says that a version of the feature is also coming to Meta Ray-Ban Display , where users can create a digital version of their face for hands-free video calls, beginning with WhatsApp.
Meta kicked off its Meta Connect 2026 event today, its yearly showcase for new AI technologies, wearables, and VR products.
The Meta VR Glasses will go on sale in spring 2027 for $1,299.99.
What do you make of Meta’s announcements?

Its popular Meta Ray-Ban glasses are now in their third generation, but two new models steal the show: a powerful, slimmed-down version of Meta's Quest headsets capable of virtual and augmented reality modes, and a camera-free pair of Ray-Ban–branded smart glasses, called Ray-Ban Meta Audio.
Instead of a heavy helmet-like headset, the new Meta VR Glasses look like big goggles.
The Meta-branded Gen 3 glasses are also on sale now for $299.
Meta says the VR Glasses cost $1,300 and will ship in the spring of 2027.
A new hearing aid feature called Hearing Enhancement uses the speakers in Meta's glasses to enhance speech and audio around the wearer, similar to the Nuance glasses from EssilorLuxottica.
Meta is also bringing its Muse AI agent to its smart glasses platform.
They’re five times lighter than the Meta Quest 3.
The Audio glasses cost $349 and are available for preorder now.
Now, it is already following them up with Gen 3 versions.

extraction.body: Its popular Meta Ray-Ban glasses are now in their third generation, but two new models steal the show: a powerful, slimmed-down version of Meta's Quest headsets capable of virtual and augmented reality modes, and a camera-free pair of Ray-Ban–branded smart glasses, called Ray-Ban Meta Audio. Meta is also bringing its Muse AI agent to its smart glasses platform. Meta VR Glasses The next evolution of Meta’s Quest VR headset is something truly different. Instead of a heavy helmet-like headset, the new Meta VR Glasses look like big goggles. They’re five times lighter than the Meta Quest 3. They sit on the nose, right in front of your face like glasses, with no headstrap needed. They look and feel more like the virtual display glasses made by companies like Viture, and what Xreal’s Project Aura seems to be shaping up to be—lightweight mixed-reality lenses that let you access virtual spaces without the burden of a VR headset. There are no included controllers, though the device can connect to Meta’s previous Quest controllers or gamepads like an Xbox controller. Form a fist and flick your thumb up or down to scroll the screen. Small prescription lens inserts can be magnetically clipped inside the lenses. (Meta has not shared how much those will cost.) The software is the same that runs on Meta’s Quest VR devices, so movie and game titles in the Quest ecosystem will work on the VR Glasses. The VR Glasses can also display a virtual keyboard on a surface in front of you, then use the embedded cameras to track specific finger placements. The only immediate downside compared to other VR headsets—at least that I could tell from a brief demo at Meta Connect—is that the VR glasses don’t cover your entire field of vision, so it doesn’t feel as immersive as a traditional VR headset. Meta says the VR Glasses cost $1,300 and will ship in the spring of 2027. Ray-Ban Meta Audio Meta has spent the past few months being absolutely pummeled by controversy about the privacy issues inherent in its camera-enabled smart glasses. The Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses have all the audio capabilities of a standard pair of Meta’s smart glasses, minus image and video capture. At 43 grams, they’re also lighter than the others. They come in 23 different color and style options, including the retro Ray-Ban Clubmaster frame and a more rectangular Burbank. The Audio glasses cost $349 and are available for preorder now. Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 Meta's flagship line of smart glasses is getting a “Gen 3” upgrade. They have 12-MP cameras, like last year, plus 3K Dolby Atmos–enabled video capture. The glasses will get up to nine hours of battery life, two more than their predecessors. A new hearing aid feature called Hearing Enhancement uses the speakers in Meta's glasses to enhance speech and audio around the wearer, similar to the Nuance glasses from EssilorLuxottica. Earlier this summer, Meta debuted smart glasses under its own branding, which cost a little less but were functionally identical to the Ray-Ban models. Now, it is already following them up with Gen 3 versions. These Meta-branded glasses come in a cat-eye shape called Capri and a rounder lens called Nova. The Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 glasses start at $449. The Meta-branded Gen 3 glasses are also on sale now for $299. Muse Charm For folks who don't wear glasses, Meta has teased a new product altogether: the Muse Charm. Zuckerberg says it's the “fastest way to talk to your Muse,” referring to the company's AI agent, and show it the world around you. That likely means it has a camera on the back. Zuckerberg says Meta still needs to finalize the hardware, but plans to have it ready by the holiday season. Meta Ray-Ban Display Meta's Display glasses are also getting some updates. With the implementation of Meta AI, users can create photorealistic holograms of their faces, which can be helpful for video calls.

sources.title: Meta introduces camera-free AI glasses
passages: Confirming earlier reports , Meta announced its first pair of camera-free AI glasses, the clunkily named Ray-Ban Meta Audio, at its Connect 2026 conference on Wednesday.

Designed to combat criticism around the more malicious use cases for AI glasses, which saw them nicknamed “pervert glasses” by some, the new devices will be audio-only, offering the ability to listen to music and podcasts, take calls, translate speech, and communicate with Meta’s AI assistant, Muse.
These will have a 12 MP camera that supports 3K Ultra HD video, a six-mic array, and up to nine hours of battery life.

While Meta today offers a range of AI glasses in a variety of styles, colors, and capabilities, the audio-only glasses could help the brand recover from some of the reputational damage after critics pointed out how people , often men , were using AI glasses to record videos without subjects’ consent.
Meta attempted to mitigate this issue with an update that would disable the camera if the LED light that indicated the glasses were recording was ever tampered with.

The glasses Meta launched with EssilorLuxottica will also see an expanded lineup of styles and colors as well as a new partnership with singer Lisa, which follows the company’s earlier brand partnership with Kylie Jenner.

The company also teased other coming updates, including support for Dolby Atmos Capture, a feature that picks the best photo from multiple frames, an option to choose landscape or portrait modes, hearing enhancements for those with hearing loss, more detailed responses, different audio modes, customizable controls, and something called “private processing” that Meta claims will prevent the company from seeing your data.

sources.title: YouTube Music is testing its answer to Spotify AI DJ– and early users can’t decide it they love it or hate it - techradar.com
passages: YouTube Music's answer to Spotify's AI DJ is far from perfect and is still a beta experiment.
But with a few tweaks here and there it could surface as one of the music streamer's best features.
Based on the early reactions from test users, there’s hope for the service’s venture into AI-based experiences – as long as YouTube listens to that user feedback.
Instead, some have credited it for its natural interjections and unintrusive commentary.
The voices themselves have also been praised, but more seem to be in favor of the female host rather than the male host.

When Spotify rolled out AI DJ in 2023, it sparked a huge debate about AI’s presence within music streaming, but was also criticized – especially for its lack of new music recommendations and jarring voiceover.
I was one of those critics, but warmed up to it when Spotify introduced its song requests feature .
It’s still in its infancy, but users are already gathering their thoughts.
Though YouTube Music’s new feature has largely gone down well, it isn't the biggest feature that users have been asking for.
Others simply hate the concept in general, with Reddit user 'ptrckl_' stating "I just wanna listen to my music".

In addition to other basic functions such as searching within playlists and volume normalization, some have noted that YouTube has yet to introduce a ‘liked songs’ library, a simple feature on other major platforms.

sources.title: YouTube Music gets more conversational with new AI features
passages: YouTube is adding new AI-powered features to YouTube Music that aim to make it easier for listeners to discover music, explore artists, and find podcasts they may otherwise miss.
Built directly into the YouTube Music app, Ask Music lets users describe what they want to hear in everyday language rather than searching for individual songs or artists.
The feature works across YouTube Music’s catalog of more than 300 million songs, including official recordings, remixes, live performances, covers, and DJ sets.
Users can use it to build custom listening queues, explore an artist’s motivations, or dig deeper into music history.
The new features are part of YouTube’s broader push to use AI throughout its services.
YouTube Music is also introducing Your Podcast Lineup, a personalized AI-generated audio guide for podcast discovery.
Each week, it will provide a short spoken preview of recommended shows and explain why they might appeal to the listener.
It can then move directly into suggested episodes.

coreStoryFacts.text: YouTube Music is rolling out some fun new features, including the expansion of the "hum to search" tool that has been in beta for Android users since March.
It's also been working on something called AI-generated conversational radio.
This isn't a platform in which AI DJs take jobs away from Wolfman Jack or whatever.
Rather, it's a tool that lets people use natural conversation to describe the type of radio station they want to listen to.
The algorithm will take in that information and create some tailor-made radio.
This is sort of like Spotify's AI DJ from a while back , but the conversational element should make the algorithm zero in on your exact tastes as described.
YouTube Music today is making official sound search, while acknowledging that it’s testing the “AI-generated conversational radio” for US Premium subscribers.
It lets you create a custom radio by “describing exactly what they want to hear.”
It simply lets you query YTM’s “catalog of over 100 million official songs by sound.” Some users had it in May before the feature was rolled back for whatever reason.

Once available, you can tap the magnifying glass icon in the top-right corner of YouTube Music to access a waveform button. (It appears next to the existing microphone for voice search.) This launches a fullscreen UI that lets you sing, hum, or play a song.
Check out 9to5Google on YouTube for more news:
YouTube Music's answer to Spotify's AI DJ is far from perfect and is still a beta experiment.
But with a few tweaks here and there it could surface as one of the music streamer's best features.
Based on the early reactions from test users, there’s hope for the service’s venture into AI-based experiences – as long as YouTube listens to that user feedback.
Instead, some have credited it for its natural interjections and unintrusive commentary.
The voices themselves have also been praised, but more seem to be in favor of the female host rather than the male host.

When Spotify rolled out AI DJ in 2023, it sparked a huge debate about AI’s presence within music streaming, but was also criticized – especially for its lack of new music recommendations and jarring voiceover.
I was one of those critics, but warmed up to it when Spotify introduced its song requests feature .
It’s still in its infancy, but users are already gathering their thoughts.
Though YouTube Music’s new feature has largely gone down well, it isn't the biggest feature that users have been asking for.
Others simply hate the concept in general, with Reddit user 'ptrckl_' stating "I just wanna listen to my music".

sources.title: YouTube Music gets more conversational with new AI features
passages: YouTube is adding new AI-powered features to YouTube Music that aim to make it easier for listeners to discover music, explore artists, and find podcasts they may otherwise miss.
Built directly into the YouTube Music app, Ask Music lets users describe what they want to hear in everyday language rather than searching for individual songs or artists.
The feature works across YouTube Music’s catalog of more than 300 million songs, including official recordings, remixes, live performances, covers, and DJ sets.
Users can use it to build custom listening queues, explore an artist’s motivations, or dig deeper into music history.
The new features are part of YouTube’s broader push to use AI throughout its services.
YouTube Music is also introducing Your Podcast Lineup, a personalized AI-generated audio guide for podcast discovery.
Each week, it will provide a short spoken preview of recommended shows and explain why they might appeal to the listener.
It can then move directly into suggested episodes.

extraction.body: YouTube is adding new AI-powered features to YouTube Music that aim to make it easier for listeners to discover music, explore artists, and find podcasts they may otherwise miss. Announced at this year’s Made On YouTube event, the updates include “Ask Music,” a conversational tool for music and podcasts, and “Your Podcast Lineup,” a personalized audio guide designed to help listeners discover new shows. Built directly into the YouTube Music app, Ask Music lets users describe what they want to hear in everyday language rather than searching for individual songs or artists. The feature works across YouTube Music’s catalog of more than 300 million songs, including official recordings, remixes, live performances, covers, and DJ sets. Users can use it to build custom listening queues, explore an artist’s motivations, or dig deeper into music history. YouTube explains that, instead of manually searching, the user simply types the request as if they were asking a friend. For instance, someone could ask Ask Music to create a mix based on the tracks that inspired a particular song. Users can also ask other questions, such as who played bass on a particular song or other details about its creation. YouTube Music is also introducing Your Podcast Lineup, a personalized AI-generated audio guide for podcast discovery. The feature is designed for a familiar problem: There are more podcasts than most people have time to listen to. Even listeners who already have a list of favorite shows can struggle to keep up with new episodes, let alone find new ones. Your Podcast Lineup will appear on the podcast page in the YouTube Music app. Each week, it will provide a short spoken preview of recommended shows and explain why they might appeal to the listener. It can then move directly into suggested episodes. Spotify recently introduced an AI-powered feature that follows a similar direction. Its personal podcasts feature uses AI to generate podcast episodes based on their interests and prompts. The new features are part of YouTube’s broader push to use AI throughout its services. Last year, YouTube Music experimented with AI-powered music hosts that provide stories, fan trivia, and commentary related to what users are listening to. Both updates are coming soon to YouTube Music and YouTube Premium subscribers worldwide. sources.title: Meta is working on making Muse its smart glasses assistant - Android Authority
passages: Meta is preparing to make its new AI agent Muse the brains behind its smart glasses, potentially replacing the standard Meta AI with a significantly more autonomous assistant.
A separate leak shared by Wong on X shows Meta is also working on “Meta Pay for Muse,” developing a native wallet interface for Muse with Meta Pay support, alongside Stripe’s Link and Shop Pay.
The integration appears designed to enable the agent to execute real-world transactions and make secure purchases on a user’s behalf.

The leaked setup screen, titled “Enable Impacc as your glasses assistant?” (where “Impacc” likely refers to an internal codename for Muse), notes that Muse is in beta and will allow users to swap back to Meta AI whenever they prefer.

Interestingly, the prompt explicitly lists features that are not yet available in the beta, tipping Meta’s hand on what is coming: Live AI, Navigation, Shazam song identification, Strava, and Health Connect integrations.
The move fits cleanly alongside Meta’s broader hardware roadmap.
The company currently dominates the market for smart-glasses shipments , and recent reports indicate it is exploring camera-free smart glasses focused entirely on ambient voice interactions .
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission.

Adding turn-by-turn navigation and fitness-tracking capabilities would transform Meta’s eyewear from a passive conversational accessory into an active, hands-free personal enabler device, just like your phone.
Wearers could perhaps track a run in Strava or ask the glasses to guide them home entirely by voice.

passages: Meta says it is bringing Muse computer work to Mac.
The company had previously talked about Muse coming to Mac , and spent more time on Wednesday providing a few new details.
This means that users will be able to delegate tasks to the agent, and — much like other popular AI agents from OpenAI and Anthropic — Muse will be able to operate any app on a user’s desktop.
Meta’s personal AI agent Muse is only a few weeks old, and the social networking giant isn’t wasting any time building out what may be its biggest bet on consumer AI to date.
The agent is powered by Muse Spark , Meta’s multimodal AI model built for agentic work.
Meta has touted it as a more accessible agent than those offered by competitors — an AI helper that, from the jump, allows users to automate the busy work in their lives.
Muse will also be integrated with Meta’s smart glasses line , the company announced.
Wang noted that the company wants Muse to connect with small business too.

Meta recently opened its platform to allow developers to build their own “connectors.” The company received more than 1,500 applications in less than week, he said, adding “I think this could be a generational opportunity to start building for a new platform as it takes off, and the response so far has been really great.”
Meta said Muse will work in the background and check back in when it’s done.

Muse can access the entire Shopify product catalog agentically and use Lync and now Shop Pay to buy almost anything on the internet, according to Wang, who noted that Meta has also added more support for payments with PayPal.
The Muse agent (the physical avatar is named Jolly, according to Zuckerberg) is designed to handle everyday tasks by connecting to users’ apps and services, including email and calendars.
At Connect, Zuckerberg introduced a slew of new capabilities and integrations to make Muse more useful and more deeply woven into users’ daily lives.

“The centerpiece of our vision for what we’re building is Muse,” Zuckerberg said as he kicked off a keynote donning khakis and a black T-shirt with the words “Building is My love Language” emblazoned across the front. “In the coming years, I expect that Muse is going to grow into the personal superintelligence that billions of people around the world are going to use to accomplish their goals and improve their lives.”
Zuckerberg also believes that Muse will make money for its users — and of course, eventually for Meta.
Meta’s Wang announced it is developing that feature and will make it available “soon,” without providing a more precise timeline.
There’s certainly a hint of Metaverse-ishness to this feature, which was demoed on stage at Connect.

passages: Muse is just one of several major updates coming to Meta’s glasses.
Just a couple of weeks after launching Muse, Meta announced that it’s “working on” bringing the agent to its smart glasses, including the new glasses it unveiled at Meta Connect.

They’re also getting some new accessibility features, like a Hearing Enhancement feature Meta says is “FDA-cleared software for adults with perceived mild to moderate hearing loss.” It will be available later this year with a Meta One subscription or as a $149 add-on for compatible glasses.
A new audio customization feature will also allow users to shift their smart glasses’ volume between their left and right ears, including sending all audio to one side.
The Meta Ray-Ban Display will also start using “the world in front of you rather than street signs in turn-by-turn walking directions,” like referencing a house, car, or landmark the glasses detect.

extraction.body: Just a couple of weeks after launching Muse, Meta announced that it’s “working on” bringing the agent to its smart glasses, including the new glasses it unveiled at Meta Connect. Users will be able to activate Muse from their glasses by saying its name and ask it to handle tasks like guiding a workout, logging meals, or helping them shop for products they’re looking at. Muse is just one of several major updates coming to Meta’s glasses. They’re also getting some new accessibility features, like a Hearing Enhancement feature Meta says is “FDA-cleared software for adults with perceived mild to moderate hearing loss.” It will be available later this year with a Meta One subscription or as a $149 add-on for compatible glasses. Meta AI will also be able to give “more context-rich answers” when users ask the glasses what they’re looking at, potentially making Meta’s glasses more effective for helping blind and low-vision users interpret their surroundings. A new audio customization feature will also allow users to shift their smart glasses’ volume between their left and right ears, including sending all audio to one side. Meta’s introducing some new audio and photo features as well, including Dolby Atmos Capture, which will allow users to record videos with 360-degree spatial audio. A new Dynamic Photo feature automatically captures multiple frames when you take a photo with Meta’s glasses, then uses Meta AI to suggest the best frame from each batch. The Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses are getting the new “Hologram” feature Meta announced for its new VR Glasses, which it says is “a photorealistic digital version of your face for calls from Meta Ray-Ban Display” that “infers” your expression using your voice. The feature’s “rolling out in Early Access on WhatsApp to Meta Ray-Ban Display users in the US later this fall.” A couple new heads-up navigation features are coming to the Meta Ray-Ban Display as well. The Meta Ray-Ban Display will also start using “the world in front of you rather than street signs in turn-by-turn walking directions,” like referencing a house, car, or landmark the glasses detect. A few other new features are on the way for the Display glasses, including an option for editing photos directly on the glasses’ display, a new “Explore” app for finding new apps, an improved calendar, and mirroring for phone notifications.

extraction.body: Meta Platforms NASDAQ: META used its Connect event to outline an expanded artificial intelligence strategy centered on Muse, a personal agent the company said is designed to help users complete tasks, manage information and interact across devices. The event’s keynote speaker described personal superintelligence as a technology that could give users “an extremely capable personal agent” that understands their goals and can work on their behalf. Meta said its approach is to distribute the technology broadly, rather than concentrate it among a small number of organizations. Muse, which Meta said it shipped several weeks ago, is intended to evolve into a personal agent used by billions of people. The company said each Muse has its own private and secure virtual machine, or Muse secure VM, and that the Muse Spark model is trained specifically for personal-agent tasks. Muse expands across shopping, productivity and devices Alexandr Wang, Meta’s Chief AI Officer, said the company has rolled out Muse in Canada and plans to bring it to additional countries. Meta recently launched a Muse Mac app that can work across users’ files, messages, calendars and notes, according to Wang. Meta also announced Computer Vision capabilities for Muse on Mac. With a user’s permission, Wang said, the agent will be able to operate apps on the computer and continue working on queued tasks while the user is away. The company is also developing an email capability that would allow users to add Muse to an email thread or forward emails for it to handle. The company highlighted an expanding network of connectors that link Muse to external services. Existing and newly announced partners discussed at the event included Spotify, OpenTable, Plaid, Ticketmaster, Stripe, Shopify, PayPal, Expedia, Instacart, Box, GitHub, Granola and Notion. Wang said Walmart, Best Buy, Gap, Sephora and Wayfair are integrating with Muse for shopping experiences. He added that Meta opened its Connector Platform to developers the prior week and had received more than 1,500 applications. Meta said Muse will be free for a large number of tokens, with the company expecting over time to profit by taking a small fee from transactions. Wang said Meta’s models are optimized for agentic behavior, including remembering preferences, personalizing actions, selecting tools and chaining actions across applications and services. AI features headed to Meta glasses The keynote speaker said Meta plans in the coming weeks to upgrade the AI experience on Meta Glasses, enabling users to hold ongoing voice conversations with their Muse rather than receive only a single response to a request. The agent will retain context from prior discussions and work in the background, the company said. Meta also emphasized privacy and security features. The company said it plans to introduce a Muse confidential VM that would prevent Meta from seeing user information. It is also building private processing for glasses, which it said will allow certain AI features to run in a secure server environment where neither Meta nor others can access users’ data. Meta said it will begin rolling out the technology for features such as live translation. In addition, Meta announced Hearing Enhancement, an FDA-cleared over-the-counter hearing aid feature designed to compensate for perceived mild to moderate hearing loss. Users will be able to take a guided assessment in the companion app and tune amplification to their hearing needs, according to the company. Broader glasses lineup Meta introduced a new audio-glasses category without cameras, which it said enables lighter and slimmer designs and all-day battery life. The company also updated its Ray-Ban Meta line with Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3, featuring slimmer frames and temples, adjustable temple tips, updated battery performance, additional capture modes, Dolby Atmos spatial audio capture and six microphones. The company said it is adding Clubmaster, Aviator and Zena models to its lineup, along with expanded style options. Meta said it will offer 51 style combinations, including an Adventurer style starting at $249. It also announced a glasses collaboration with rapper and singer Lisa Manobal of Blackpink. Meta said its Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses, which include full-color displays and the Meta Neural Band, will become available online through meta.com and begin an international rollout. By the end of the year, the company expects to offer more than 100 glasses styles. Meta VR Glasses set for spring launch The company also unveiled Meta VR Glasses, a roughly 100-gram device that it said delivers high-resolution immersive displays in a glasses form factor. The product is designed to serve as a private cinema, a multi-monitor computer and a gaming device. Andrew Bosworth, Meta’s Chief Technology Officer, said the device is IMAX Enhanced certified and supports Dolby Atmos spatial audio and Dolby Vision. It will support the Quest library with optional controllers, Xbox Cloud Gaming, and 75 hands-only titles at launch, according to Bosworth. Meta said Disney+, Peacock, Paramount+, HBO Max, YouTube, Prime Video and Crunchyroll will offer content on the platform. The company also said it plans more than 100 immersive sports events per year, including ESPN programming beginning with college football on Quest this fall. Meta VR Glasses are scheduled to ship in the spring for $1,299. Finally, Meta previewed Muse Charm, a keychain-sized device designed to provide quick access to the Muse experience through a fingerprint sensor, voice interaction and a camera. The company said it expects Muse Charm to be ready to ship in December and plans to provide additional details later. About Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) Meta Platforms, Inc develops technologies that help people connect, communicate and build communities online. The company's principal products include Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp and Threads, which enable social networking, messaging, content sharing and digital communication. Meta generates most of its business through advertising displayed across its family of apps. It also develops artificial intelligence technologies, business messaging tools and hardware and software through its Reality Labs division, including Quest virtual- and mixed-reality devices and related experiences. The company was founded as Facebook in 2004 by Mark Zuckerberg and was renamed Meta Platforms in 2021 to reflect its broader focus on building the metaverse. The company highlighted an expanding network of connectors that link Muse to external services. Existing and newly announced partners discussed at the event included Spotify, OpenTable, Plaid, Ticketmaster, Stripe, Shopify, PayPal, Expedia, Instacart, Box, GitHub, Granola and Notion.

Wang said Walmart, Best Buy, Gap, Sephora and Wayfair are integrating with Muse for shopping experiences. He added that Meta opened its Connector Platform to developers the prior week and had received more than 1,500 applications.

Meta said Muse will be free for a large number of tokens, with the company expecting over time to profit by taking a small fee from transactions. Wang said Meta’s models are optimized for agentic behavior, including remembering preferences, personalizing actions, selecting tools and chaining actions across applications and services. AI features headed to Meta glasses The keynote speaker said Meta plans in the coming weeks to upgrade the AI experience on Meta Glasses, enabling users to hold ongoing voice conversations with their Muse rather than receive only a single response to a request. The agent will retain context from prior discussions and work in the background, the company said.

Meta also emphasized privacy and security features. The company said it plans to introduce a Muse confidential VM that would prevent Meta from seeing user information. It is also building private processing for glasses, which it said will allow certain AI features to run in a secure server environment where neither Meta nor others can access users’ data. Meta said it will begin rolling out the technology for features such as live translation.

In addition, Meta announced Hearing Enhancement, an FDA-cleared over-the-counter hearing aid feature designed to compensate for perceived mild to moderate hearing loss. Users will be able to take a guided assessment in the companion app and tune amplification to their hearing needs, according to the company. Broader glasses lineup Meta introduced a new audio-glasses category without cameras, which it said enables lighter and slimmer designs and all-day battery life. The company also updated its Ray-Ban Meta line with Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3, featuring slimmer frames and temples, adjustable temple tips, updated battery performance, additional capture modes, Dolby Atmos spatial audio capture and six microphones.

The company said it is adding Clubmaster, Aviator and Zena models to its lineup, along with expanded style options. Meta said it will offer 51 style combinations, including an Adventurer style starting at $249. It also announced a glasses collaboration with rapper and singer Lisa Manobal of Blackpink.

Meta said its Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses, which include full-color displays and the Meta Neural Band, will become available online through meta.com and begin an international rollout. By the end of the year, the company expects to offer more than 100 glasses styles. Meta VR Glasses set for spring launch The company also unveiled Meta VR Glasses, a roughly 100-gram device that it said delivers high-resolution immersive displays in a glasses form factor. The product is designed to serve as a private cinema, a multi-monitor computer and a gaming device.

Andrew Bosworth, Meta’s Chief Technology Officer, said the device is IMAX Enhanced certified and supports Dolby Atmos spatial audio and Dolby Vision. It will support the Quest library with optional controllers, Xbox Cloud Gaming, and 75 hands-only titles at launch, according to Bosworth.

Meta said Disney+, Peacock, Paramount+, HBO Max, YouTube, Prime Video and Crunchyroll will offer content on the platform. The company also said it plans more than 100 immersive sports events per year, including ESPN programming beginning with college football on Quest this fall.
Meta VR Glasses are scheduled to ship in the spring for $1,299.

Finally, Meta previewed Muse Charm, a keychain-sized device designed to provide quick access to the Muse experience through a fingerprint sensor, voice interaction and a camera. The company said it expects Muse Charm to be ready to ship in December and plans to provide additional details later. About Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) Meta Platforms, Inc develops technologies that help people connect, communicate and build communities online. The company's principal products include Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp and Threads, which enable social networking, messaging, content sharing and digital communication.

Meta generates most of its business through advertising displayed across its family of apps. It also develops artificial intelligence technologies, business messaging tools and hardware and software through its Reality Labs division, including Quest virtual- and mixed-reality devices and related experiences.

coreStoryFacts.text: Meta is preparing to make its new AI agent Muse the brains behind its smart glasses, potentially replacing the standard Meta AI with a significantly more autonomous assistant.
A separate leak shared by Wong on X shows Meta is also working on “Meta Pay for Muse,” developing a native wallet interface for Muse with Meta Pay support, alongside Stripe’s Link and Shop Pay.
The integration appears designed to enable the agent to execute real-world transactions and make secure purchases on a user’s behalf.

The leaked setup screen, titled “Enable Impacc as your glasses assistant?” (where “Impacc” likely refers to an internal codename for Muse), notes that Muse is in beta and will allow users to swap back to Meta AI whenever they prefer.

Interestingly, the prompt explicitly lists features that are not yet available in the beta, tipping Meta’s hand on what is coming: Live AI, Navigation, Shazam song identification, Strava, and Health Connect integrations.
The move fits cleanly alongside Meta’s broader hardware roadmap.
The company currently dominates the market for smart-glasses shipments , and recent reports indicate it is exploring camera-free smart glasses focused entirely on ambient voice interactions .
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission.

Adding turn-by-turn navigation and fitness-tracking capabilities would transform Meta’s eyewear from a passive conversational accessory into an active, hands-free personal enabler device, just like your phone.
Wearers could perhaps track a run in Strava or ask the glasses to guide them home entirely by voice.
Meta says it is bringing Muse computer work to Mac.
The company had previously talked about Muse coming to Mac , and spent more time on Wednesday providing a few new details.
This means that users will be able to delegate tasks to the agent, and — much like other popular AI agents from OpenAI and Anthropic — Muse will be able to operate any app on a user’s desktop.
Meta’s personal AI agent Muse is only a few weeks old, and the social networking giant isn’t wasting any time building out what may be its biggest bet on consumer AI to date.
The agent is powered by Muse Spark , Meta’s multimodal AI model built for agentic work.
Meta has touted it as a more accessible agent than those offered by competitors — an AI helper that, from the jump, allows users to automate the busy work in their lives.
Muse will also be integrated with Meta’s smart glasses line , the company announced.
Wang noted that the company wants Muse to connect with small business too.

Meta recently opened its platform to allow developers to build their own “connectors.” The company received more than 1,500 applications in less than week, he said, adding “I think this could be a generational opportunity to start building for a new platform as it takes off, and the response so far has been really great.”
Meta said Muse will work in the background and check back in when it’s done.

Muse can access the entire Shopify product catalog agentically and use Lync and now Shop Pay to buy almost anything on the internet, according to Wang, who noted that Meta has also added more support for payments with PayPal.
The Muse agent (the physical avatar is named Jolly, according to Zuckerberg) is designed to handle everyday tasks by connecting to users’ apps and services, including email and calendars.
At Connect, Zuckerberg introduced a slew of new capabilities and integrations to make Muse more useful and more deeply woven into users’ daily lives.

“The centerpiece of our vision for what we’re building is Muse,” Zuckerberg said as he kicked off a keynote donning khakis and a black T-shirt with the words “Building is My love Language” emblazoned across the front. “In the coming years, I expect that Muse is going to grow into the personal superintelligence that billions of people around the world are going to use to accomplish their goals and improve their lives.”

At Connect, Zuckerberg introduced a slew of new capabilities and integrations to make Muse more useful and more deeply woven into users’ daily lives. Here are the new features and capabilities that got our attention … One of the more fun announcements made Wednesday is that Muse users will soon have the ability to conjure a distinct digital avatar for their particular agent and then video chat with it in real time. A new AI model, Muse Realtime Avatar, has been developed to power the particular feature, the company says. The idea is that Meta’s previously faceless AI software will be given a face, body, and voice, making them significantly more personable. There’s certainly a hint of Metaverse-ishness to this feature, which was demoed on stage at Connect. Users will be able to have live conversations with this avatar, giving it tasks and asking it questions. Muse will also be integrated with Meta’s smart glasses line , the company announced. This means that users will be able to communicate with their agent merely by speaking to their glasses. The agent activates via a wake word, the company said, adding that it will be able to guide users through a personalized workout, log meals, book an appointment, and help them buy products they see. Meta’s Wang announced it is developing that feature and will make it available “soon,” without providing a more precise timeline. Users will also be able to add Muse to an email thread or forward emails from the agent to handle on their behalf. Meta has touted it as a more accessible agent than those offered by competitors — an AI helper that, from the jump, allows users to automate the busy work in their lives.
Muse will also be integrated with Meta’s smart glasses line , the company announced.
Wang noted that the company wants Muse to connect with small business too.

Meta recently opened its platform to allow developers to build their own “connectors.” The company received more than 1,500 applications in less than week, he said, adding “I think this could be a generational opportunity to start building for a new platform as it takes off, and the response so far has been really great.”
Meta said Muse will work in the background and check back in when it’s done.

Muse can access the entire Shopify product catalog agentically and use Lync and now Shop Pay to buy almost anything on the internet, according to Wang, who noted that Meta has also added more support for payments with PayPal.
The Muse agent (the physical avatar is named Jolly, according to Zuckerberg) is designed to handle everyday tasks by connecting to users’ apps and services, including email and calendars.
At Connect, Zuckerberg introduced a slew of new capabilities and integrations to make Muse more useful and more deeply woven into users’ daily lives.

“The centerpiece of our vision for what we’re building is Muse,” Zuckerberg said as he kicked off a keynote donning khakis and a black T-shirt with the words “Building is My love Language” emblazoned across the front. “In the coming years, I expect that Muse is going to grow into the personal superintelligence that billions of people around the world are going to use to accomplish their goals and improve their lives.”
Zuckerberg also believes that Muse will make money for its users — and of course, eventually for Meta.
Meta’s Wang announced it is developing that feature and will make it available “soon,” without providing a more precise timeline.
There’s certainly a hint of Metaverse-ishness to this feature, which was demoed on stage at Connect.

Meta AI will also be able to give “more context-rich answers” when users ask the glasses what they’re looking at, potentially making Meta’s glasses more effective for helping blind and low-vision users interpret their surroundings. A new audio customization feature will also allow users to shift their smart glasses’ volume between their left and right ears, including sending all audio to one side. Meta’s introducing some new audio and photo features as well, including Dolby Atmos Capture, which will allow users to record videos with 360-degree spatial audio. The Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses are getting the new “Hologram” feature Meta announced for its new VR Glasses, which it says is “a photorealistic digital version of your face for calls from Meta Ray-Ban Display” that “infers” your expression using your voice. The Meta Ray-Ban Display will also start using “the world in front of you rather than street signs in turn-by-turn walking directions,” like referencing a house, car, or landmark the glasses detect. A few other new features are on the way for the Display glasses, including an option for editing photos directly on the glasses’ display, a new “Explore” app for finding new apps, an improved calendar, and mirroring for phone notifications.
